text.t: Effect of temperature on the rate of reaction between sodium thiosulfate and hydrochloric acid
Amira Hassan, with Tom Reilly · Year 12 · Marked by Dr Lowe · 14 October

The time for a cross to disappear was recorded at five temperatures from 20 to 60 °C. Rate roughly doubled for every 10 °C rise, supporting collision theory. Uncertainty was dominated by judging the end point by eye.
To find how temperature affects reaction rate.
rate will increase with temperature because more collisions exceed the activation energy.
Measure 50 cm³ of 0.1 M Na₂S₂O₃ into a flask.
Warm in a water bath to the target temperature.
Add 5 cm³ of 1 M HCl and start the timer.
Stop when the cross is no longer visible from above.
Repeat three times at each temperature.
Worked example at 40 °C: rate = 1 ÷ 35 s = 0.0286 s⁻¹.
The hypothesis is supported: rate increased with temperature and approximately doubled per 10 °C. The trend fits collision theory, within the ±2 s reading uncertainty.

Income, tastes, price of substitutes, expectations. A change in the good's own price is a movement
Avian flu cut supply: the curve moved left. Demand is inelastic, so price rose far more than quantity fell.

Cities thrive on mixed uses and short blocks, because safety and vitality come from people, not from planning.
